recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Any future change in this area should be handled against current ServiceRequest/workflow/Event pattern source rather than retired ReferralRequest wording.
issue_request: FHIR-6195 asked for a reference to fulfillment of a ReferralRequest, including when the request was fulfilled or when the requested service occurred. The Published Not Persuasive with Modification resolution said fulfillment resources should point to ReferralRequest rather than vice versa, with related-resource documentation noting Encounter, Procedure, DiagnosticReport, or other assessment-related fulfillment resources.
initial_application: Commit a7344a39aa35eeb8f52cb6d13a8e63eabd6105b2 added ReferralRequest introduction prose saying ReferralRequest might be fulfilled by DiagnosticReport, Encounter, Procedure, or other assessment-related resources. A nearby DiagnosticReport history commit, d543702d19ed5858e25cea2f9c4942e0c2ec964b, widened DiagnosticReport.request to include ReferralRequest.
additional_context: FHIR-13196 later merged ReferralRequest and ProcedureRequest into the current ServiceRequest resource; source/fhir.ini lists ServiceRequest as active and notes ReferralRequest became ServiceRequest. FHIR-13195 later renamed incomingReferral-style links to basedOn. The current ServiceRequest page and Request pattern state that generated Event resources link back to requests through basedOn, while Encounter, DiagnosticReport, Procedure, and Observation basedOn definitions target ServiceRequest.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current build already conveys the required directionality and fulfillment-resource linkage through active build-scope source, so adding another ServiceRequest paragraph would be redundant.

related_jiras.note: Merged ReferralRequest and ProcedureRequest into ServiceRequest, establishing the current artifact that carries the referral-request behavior.
Renamed Appointment and Encounter incomingReferral to basedOn after the ServiceRequest merge, reinforcing the current basedOn direction.
A contemporaneous Procedure/DiagnosticReport boundary discussion referenced FHIR-6195 but did not require a separate current-source decision here.
